Verbs with Infinitives in Affirmative, Negative and Interrogative Statements
In English, there are some infinitive verbs that are always followed by other verbs such as the verb have.

These verbs always have the preposition to after them and they can express different meanings. When you use the infinitive verb have, it refers to the purpose of doing something:
I have to write a code using HTLM server controls.
You can use verbs with infinitives in negative and interrogative statements too, for instance:

I don't have to write a code using HTLM server controls.
Do you have to write a code using HTLM sever controls?
There are some other meanings when using infinitive verbs such as:

  • Verbs that express thinking or feeling: decide, choose, hope, like, prefer, expect, etc.
  • Verbs of speaking: promise, agree, refuse, etc.
  • Other verbs: want, help, try, need, manage, plan, need etc.

Max: Hey, Pete! What are you doing?
Peter: I'm trying to do an assignment for Mr. Simmons class. I have to write a code to give an example of HTLM server controls for ASP.NET.
Max: HTLM server controls? Are those the buttons we often use in a graphical user interface?
Peter: Yes. You know, they are based on the standard HTLM controls but server controls make server-side processing possible.
Max: Are header tags and input elements server-side controls too?
Peter: Not really, those elements don't have to be processed by the server.

Max: So, do server controls have any advantage compared to standard controls?
Peter: When you choose to use server controls, you can enable static tables for layout purposes. Besides that, you are allowed to transform HTLM pages to make them run in the ASP.NET framework.
Max: I see. What do you have to do to add an HTLM server control?
Peter: Well, when you have to use an element as a control, you normally have to write the HTLM syntax of the element, but in addition to this, you proceed to add a runat="server" attribute.
Max: You can't forget to code the ID attribute of each element.
Peter: You're right! The ID attribute helps to have access to the controls' content programmatically.

Max: What kind of HTLM server control names do you know?
Peter: Well, there are many, for instance, HtmlInputFile, its HTLM tag is < input type = file >. HtmlInputImage, < input type = image >; HtmlTitle, < title > element, etc.
Max: That's hard to remember! What do you plan to create for your assignment?
Peter: I want to create a basic HTLM table to get basic information from the users, it is like a form…
